definition_zh: 可理解的；易懂的；只用理智可认识的
definition_en: able to be understood, especially when speech or writing is clear enough to follow
core_image: 一句话落进耳朵，听者一下子拼出了完整意思
scene: 讲座结束后，有学生说客座讲师的发言不能完全听清。After the lecture, some students said the guest speaker was not entirely intelligible.
sceneCN: 这里 intelligible 是「可理解的」（第 1 个义项：话说得让人听得懂、能明白）；句意：讲座结束后，有学生说那位客座讲师的发言并不能完全听懂。

pos.zh: 可理解的；易懂的；可领会的

derivatives.zh: intelligible 加名词后缀 -ity 构成，义为「可理解性；清晰度」
intelligible 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「可理解地；明白地」
加否定前缀 un- 构成，义为「难以理解的；听不清的」

senses.title: Able to be understood
senses.definition: clear and easy enough to be understood
senses.definitionCN: 清楚明白，足以让人听懂或看懂
senses.example: His explanation was clear and intelligible to everyone.
senses.exampleCN: 他的解释清楚明白，人人都能听懂。
senses.why: The word comes from a Latin verb that means to understand, so intelligible names something the mind can pick up and hold.
senses.whyCN: 这个词源自表示「理解」的拉丁语动词，所以 intelligible 指心智能够接住并把握的东西。

senses.title: Clear enough to be heard
senses.definition: spoken clearly enough for a listener to catch the words, even if the meaning is hard
senses.definitionCN: 说话清楚到听者能捕捉到字词，即使意思较难
senses.example: The recording was old, and the voice was barely intelligible.
senses.exampleCN: 录音很旧，那个声音勉强才能听清。
senses.why: If the mind must understand it, the sound first has to reach the mind, so intelligible is also used of speech that stays audible and clear.
senses.whyCN: 既然要靠心智去理解，声音首先得清清楚楚传到心智，所以这个词也用来形容话听得清、字音不含糊。

senses.title: Knowable by the intellect
senses.definition: able to be grasped by reason or the intellect, as opposed to the senses
senses.definitionCN: 可以由理性或理智把握，而非只靠感官把握
senses.example: In the old philosophy, beauty was a quality intelligible to reason alone.
senses.exampleCN: 在旧哲学里，美被看作唯有理性才能认识的特质。
senses.why: The Latin source is tied to intellect, the power of understanding, so in formal philosophy intelligible names what the mind alone can know.
senses.whyCN: 它的拉丁语来源与 intellect（理智、理解力）相连，因此在正式哲学语境里，intelligible 指只有理智才能认识的对象。

intro.en: Intelligible comes from Latin intelligibilis, formed from intelligere (to understand); a form with a g is also attested in Latin, and it reached English through French in the fourteenth century.
intro.cn: intelligible 来自拉丁语 intelligibilis，由 intelligere（理解）派生；拉丁语中也有带 g 的拼写变体，十四世纪经法语进入英语。

items.en: Intelligere joins inter (between) and legere (to pick, to choose), and means to understand.
items.cn: intelligere 由 inter（在……之间）与 legere（挑选、择取）合成，意为「理解」。

items.en: The adjective intelligibilis means able to be understood; a variant intellegibilis with a g also occurs.
items.cn: 形容词 intelligibilis 意为「可被理解的」；拉丁语中另有带 g 的变体 intellegibilis。

items.en: Old French intelligible carries the word toward English in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语 intelligible 在十四世纪把这个词带向英语。

items.en: English intelligible is recorded from the late fourteenth century in philosophy and translation.
items.cn: 英语 intelligible 自十四世纪后期见于哲学与翻译文献。

items.en: Modern English extends it from ideas to speech, sound, and plain writing.
items.cn: 现代英语把它从思想扩展到说话、声音与通俗文字。

note.en: Intelligible shares its root with intellect and intelligent, and it sits beside words for understanding and for being understood.
note.cn: intelligible 与 intellect、intelligent 同根，并与「理解」和「被理解」两类词相邻。

entries.definition: the ability to learn and understand
entries.definitionCN: 智力；理解力

entries.definition: good at learning and understanding
entries.definitionCN: 聪明的；有理解力的

entries.definition: the power of the mind to think and understand
entries.definitionCN: 智力；理智

entries.definition: able to be understood
entries.definitionCN: 可以理解的

entries.definition: able to be grasped fully by the mind
entries.definitionCN: 可理解的；好懂的

entries.definition: clear enough to be read easily, used of writing
entries.definitionCN: 字迹清楚易读的

normalIntro.en: Intelligible carries the same root as intellect and intelligence, so it is about the mind being able to take hold.
normalIntro.cn: intelligible 与 intellect、intelligence 同根，核心是「心智能否接住」。

normal.en: Intellect and intelligible share one root about understanding.
normal.cn: intellect 与 intelligible 共享同一个表示「理解」的词根。

normal.en: Mutually intelligible is used of two accents that people can still follow.
normal.cn: mutually intelligible 形容两种口音彼此都还能听懂。

normal.en: The adverb is intelligibly, as in speak intelligibly, meaning clearly.
normal.cn: 副词形式是 intelligibly，例如 speak intelligibly，意为说得清楚。

normal.en: Unintelligible adds un- and means not able to be understood.
normal.cn: unintelligible 加上否定前缀 un-，意为听不懂。

normal.en: Compare legible: legible is about letters on a page, intelligible about meaning.
normal.cn: 对比 legible：legible 讲字迹能否看清，intelligible 讲意思能否听懂。

abstract.en: See a listener nodding after one short sentence.
abstract.cn: 想象听者听完一句话就点头。

abstract.en: Picture words slipping out of a bad recording like sand.
abstract.cn: 想象字词像沙子一样从劣质录音里滑掉。

abstract.en: Imagine a key that fits a lock: the idea slides right in.
abstract.cn: 想象一把对得上锁孔的钥匙，念头一下就滑了进去。

examples.en: The teacher tried to make the rule intelligible to young learners.
examples.cn: 老师设法把这条规则讲得让小朋友也能懂。

examples.en: Two related languages may be mutually intelligible to some degree.
examples.cn: 两种有亲缘关系的语言在一定程度上可以彼此沟通。

examples.en: The announcement was so badly recorded that it was hardly intelligible.
examples.cn: 那条通知录得太差，几乎听不清楚。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「in + tell + ible」——能让别人听（tell）明白的，就是可理解的；这纯粹是拆字谐音联想，不是词源。

root: 拉丁语 inter（在……之间）+ legere（挑选、读）→ intelligere（理解）→ intelligibilis（可理解的）→ 古法语 intelligible → 英语 intelligible，核心义「能够被心智把握」。

sensesIntro.en: Intelligible begins with plain clarity of meaning, moves to sound that can be heard, and ends with the formal idea of what reason alone can know.
sensesIntro.cn: intelligible 从「意思清楚」出发，过渡到「声音听得清」，最后落到「唯有理智可认识」这一正式用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sentence lands in the ear and clicks into a whole meaning.
core.cn: 核心意象：一句话落进耳朵，咔哒一声拼成完整的意思。

branches.en: Clear meaning is the everyday sense.
branches.cn: 意思清楚是日常义项。

branches.en: Audible speech grows from sound reaching the mind.
branches.cn: 声音传到心智，生出「听得清」的义项。

branches.en: Reason knowing is the philosophical branch.
branches.cn: 理性认识是哲学分支。

branches.en: A clear speaker gives both hearable words and graspable meaning.
branches.cn: 说话清楚的人同时提供听得清的字音与能把住的意思。

branches.en: Both everyday understanding and pure reason rest on the same act of grasping.
branches.cn: 日常理解与纯理性认识都建立在同一个「把握」动作上。

intro.en: Intelligible is built with the Latin verb intelligere, the suffix -ible, and a plain English negation.
intro.cn: intelligible 由拉丁语动词 intelligere、后缀 -ible 以及英语否定前缀构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin inter means between and legere means to pick; together they make intelligere, to understand.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 inter 意为「在……之间」，legere 意为「挑选」，合起来构成 intelligere，意为「理解」。

items.example: The prefix inter- lies inside intelligere.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 inter- 藏在 intelligere 里面。

items.example: Legere is a common Latin verb for choosing.
items.exampleCN: legere 是拉丁语中表示挑选的常用动词。

items.example: Intelligere is the source of the -ible form.
items.exampleCN: intelligere 是 -ible 形式的来源。

items.example: The suffix -ible forms intelligible.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ible 构成 intelligible。

items.example: Intelligible keeps the Latin sense.
items.exampleCN: intelligible 保留了拉丁语含义。

items.example: She spoke intelligibly to the crowd.
items.exampleCN: 她清楚地对人群讲话。

items.example: The test measures speech intelligibility.
items.exampleCN: 这项测试测量语音清晰度。

items.example: The prefix un- forms unintelligible.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 un- 构成 unintelligible。

items.example: His words were unintelligible.
items.exampleCN: 他的话听不明白。

definition_zh: 互动的；相互作用方面的；交际性的
definition_en: relating to interaction, especially the way people or things act on each other
core_image: 两个人在对话中学着对方点头、停顿和接话
scene: 研究者录下小组讨论，专门分析成员之间的互动模式。The researchers recorded the group discussion to study its interactional patterns.
sceneCN: 这里 interactional 是「互动的」（第 3 个义项：与人与人之间的互动、交际相关的）；句意：研究者把小组讨论录下来，用来研究其中的互动规律。

pos.zh: 互动的；相互作用方面的；交际性的

derivatives.zh: interact 加名词后缀 -ion 构成，义为「互动；相互作用」，是 interactional 的直接基础词
由 inter-（在……之间）加 act（行动）构成，义为「互动；相互作用」
interactional 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「在互动层面上」，使用较少

senses.title: Relating to things acting on each other
senses.definition: connected with the way two or more things affect each other
senses.definitionCN: 与两个或多个事物相互影响的方式有关
senses.example: The team studied the interactional effects of the two chemicals.
senses.exampleCN: 研究小组研究了这两种化学品的相互作用效应。
senses.why: The base verb interact joins inter (between) and act (to do), so interactional first means belonging to things acting on one another.
senses.whyCN: 基础动词 interact 由 inter（在……之间）与 act（行动）合成，所以 interactional 首先表示属于「彼此起作用」这类情形。

senses.title: Related to interaction in general
senses.definition: of or connected with an interaction between people, groups, or systems
senses.definitionCN: 属于人或群体、系统之间互动，或与之相关的
senses.example: Interactional rules differ from one culture to another.
senses.exampleCN: 互动规则因文化而不同。
senses.why: The suffix -al turns the noun interaction into a general adjective, so the word can describe any feature of any interaction.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -al 把名词 interaction 变成一般形容词，于是它可以描述任何互动的任何特征。

senses.title: Relating to talk between people
senses.definition: relating to the way people speak and respond to each other in conversation
senses.definitionCN: 与人们在对话中说话并彼此回应所体现的方式相关
senses.example: Silence can carry interactional meaning in ordinary conversation.
senses.exampleCN: 在日常对话里，沉默也能传达交际意义。
senses.why: In language studies, the unit of interest is the talk itself, so the adjective narrows to mean the shared work of speaking together.
senses.whyCN: 在语言研究中，关注的单位就是谈话本身，于是这个形容词收窄为指「你来我往地说话」这件事。

intro.en: Interactional is a nineteenth to twentieth century English adjective: interact plus the Latin noun suffix -ion, then the adjective suffix -al.
intro.cn: interactional 是十九至二十世纪形成的英语形容词：interact 先加拉丁语名词后缀 -ion 构成 interaction，再加形容词后缀 -al。

items.en: Inter means between, and agere means to do or drive; here it supplies act and -ion.
items.cn: 拉丁语 inter 意为「在……之间」，agere 意为「做、推动」，在此提供 act 与 -ion。

items.en: Interact is formed in English in the seventeenth century from inter and act, ending in a plain -t.
items.cn: interact 在十七世纪由 inter 与 act 在英语中合成，结尾是不发声的 t。

items.en: Interaction appears by the nineteenth century, and interactional follows as a regular adjective.
items.cn: interaction 在十九世纪已经出现，interactional 作为规则形容词随后产生。

items.en: Interactional enters the study of language and the social sciences, naming it as the shared work of talk.
items.cn: 二十世纪起，interactional 进入语言学与社会科学，指人与人对话中的共同建构。

items.en: Modern English keeps it mostly technical, in language, education, and systems research.
items.cn: 现代英语中它仍偏专业，多见于语言、教育与系统研究。

note.en: Interactional is the adjective of the interact family; its neighbours are other words for acting together and for how people talk.
note.cn: interactional 是 interact 家族的形容词，近邻词都表示「一起起作用」或「人们如何交谈」。

entries.definition: to act together and affect each other
entries.definitionCN: 互动；互相作用

entries.definition: the mutual action of two or more things
entries.definitionCN: 互动；相互作用

entries.definition: designed to allow two-way exchange
entries.definitionCN: 交互式的；互动的

entries.definition: relating to the sharing of information and ideas
entries.definitionCN: 交际的；交流的

entries.definition: relating to informal talk between people
entries.definitionCN: 会话的；交谈的

entries.definition: shared or felt by two or more sides alike
entries.definitionCN: 相互的；共同的

normalIntro.en: Interactional is a three-step build: inter, act, and -ion, plus the adjective suffix -al.
normalIntro.cn: interactional 分三步搭起来：inter、act、-ion，再加形容词后缀 -al。

normal.en: Inter means between, so interactional always involves at least two sides.
normal.cn: inter 意为「在……之间」，所以 interactional 至少涉及两方。

normal.en: Act inside the word keeps its basic sense of doing.
normal.cn: 词中的 act 保留「行动」的基本含义。

normal.en: Dropping -al leaves the noun interaction.
normal.cn: 去掉 -al，就是名词 interaction。

normal.en: Interactional skills are the habits of taking turns and listening.
normal.cn: interactional skills 指轮流说话与倾听的习惯。

normal.en: Compare interactive: interactive often describes screens and systems.
normal.cn: 对比 interactive：interactive 常用来形容屏幕和系统。

abstract.en: Picture two dancers adjusting to each other every step.
abstract.cn: 想象两位舞者每一步都在配合对方。

abstract.en: See a tennis rally where each shot answers the last.
abstract.cn: 想象一场网球对拉，每一下都回应上一下。

abstract.en: Imagine a heartbeat of turn-taking, back and forth.
abstract.cn: 想象轮流发言的节奏像心跳一样来回。

examples.en: Interactional analysis looks at how speakers repair misunderstandings.
examples.cn: 互动分析研究说话者如何修补误解。

examples.en: Teachers focus on interactional patterns within small groups.
examples.cn: 教师关注小组内部的互动模式。

examples.en: In many cultures, silence has an interactional function.
examples.cn: 在许多文化里，沉默也承担交际功能。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「inter + act + ion + al」——你（act）在我（inter）之间来回行动（act），再一层层加上 -ion 和 -al，就是「互动的」；这只是拆词联想，不是词源追溯。

root: 拉丁语 inter（在……之间）+ agere（做、推动，提供 act）→ 英语 interact（互动）→ 加 -ion 成 interaction → 加 -al 成 interactional，核心义「彼此之间的相互作用」。

sensesIntro.en: Interactional starts as an adjective for things acting on one another, widens to any interaction, and narrows in language study to talk between people.
sensesIntro.cn: interactional 先指事物彼此作用，再放宽为任何互动，之后又在语言研究中收窄为「人与人之间的交谈」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two people learning each others nods, pauses, and replies.
core.cn: 核心意象：两个人学着对方的点头、停顿与接话。

branches.en: Mutual effect between things is the oldest sense.
branches.cn: 事物之间的相互作用是最早的义项。

branches.en: Any interaction can take the adjective.
branches.cn: 任何互动都能用它作形容词。

branches.en: Talk between people is the language-study sense.
branches.cn: 人际交谈是语言研究中的义项。

branches.en: Both chemistry and culture describe effects that need two sides.
branches.cn: 化学与文化都在描述需要双方才能产生的效应。

branches.en: A general interaction becomes shared talk once a speaker is involved.
branches.cn: 一旦有说话者参与，一般的互动就成了共同交谈。

intro.en: Interactional stacks Latin inter, the verb act, and the suffixes -ion and -al; each piece is productive in English.
intro.cn: interactional 叠用了拉丁语 inter、动词 act 以及后缀 -ion 与 -al，每一部分在英语中都能继续构词。

latinIntro.en: Latin inter means between and agere means to do; English builds interact, interaction, and interactional on them in turn.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 inter 意为「在……之间」，agere 意为「做」，英语依次在其上造出 interact、interaction 与 interactional。

items.example: The prefix inter- fixes the between-ness.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 inter- 确定了「之间」的方向。

items.example: Act supplies the doing.
items.exampleCN: act 提供「做」的部分。

items.example: The two groups interact daily.
items.exampleCN: 这两个群体每天互动。

items.meaningCN: 表示动作或状态的名词后缀
items.example: The suffix -ion forms interaction.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ion 构成 interaction。

items.example: Interaction is the noun base.
items.exampleCN: interaction 是这个形容词的名词基础。

items.example: The suffix -al forms interactional.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -al 构成 interactional。

items.example: Interactive screens respond to touch.
items.exampleCN: 交互式屏幕触摸会回应。

items.example: The data were coded interactionally.
items.exampleCN: 这些数据按互动层面编码。

latinEntries.meaning: to act mutually, attested but rare

definition_zh: 调解；说情；代为求情
definition_en: to step in between two sides and plead on behalf of someone, especially to ask for mercy or help
core_image: 一个人走到争吵双方中间，替一个弱者向强者求情
scene: 两个孩子抢着同一件玩具，母亲走过去，替弟弟向哥哥求情。As the two boys fought over the toy, their mother walked between them and interceded on behalf of the younger one.
sceneCN: 这里 intercede 是「调解、说情」（第 1 个义项：为发生冲突的双方居中求情）；句意：两个孩子抢着同一件玩具，母亲走过去，替弟弟向哥哥求情。

pos.zh: 调解；说情；代为求情
求情；斡旋（常与 with 或 for 连用）

derivatives.zh: 由动词加名词后缀 -ion 构成，义为「求情；斡旋」
由动词加 -or 构成，义为「代为求情的人；调解人」
由 intercession 加 -ory 构成，义为「求情的；代祷的」

senses.title: To plead on behalf of someone
senses.definition: to plead with someone in power on behalf of another person, asking for mercy, help, or lenient treatment
senses.definitionCN: 向有权势者替另一个人求情，请求宽恕、帮助或宽大处理
senses.example: She interceded with the head teacher on behalf of her son.
senses.exampleCN: 她替儿子向班主任求情。
senses.why: Latin inter- means between and cedere means to go, so intercede pictures someone going between two people to speak for one of them.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 inter- 表示「在……之间」，cedere 表示「走」，所以 intercede 的画面是一个人身处两人之间，替其中一方说话。

senses.title: To step in as a mediator
senses.definition: to take part in a disagreement between two sides so as to settle it or calm it down
senses.definitionCN: 介入双方的争执，以便从中调停或平息
senses.example: The United Nations offered to intercede in the border dispute.
senses.exampleCN: 联合国表示愿在边界争端中出面斡旋。
senses.why: If the speaker stands between the two sides, the role easily widens from one favour into managing the whole quarrel.
senses.whyCN: 当说情者站在双方之间时，这个角色很容易从替一方求情，扩展为调停整场争执。

senses.title: To pray on behalf of others
senses.definition: to pray to God for another person, especially in a church setting
senses.definitionCN: 向上帝为他人祈祷，尤见于教会场合
senses.example: The priest intercedes for the sick of the parish every Sunday.
senses.exampleCN: 神父每个礼拜天都为教区的病人代祷。
senses.why: A mediator who speaks to someone in power naturally turns, in religious language, into one who speaks to God for others.
senses.whyCN: 一个向权势者说话的中间人，在宗教语言里自然变成向上帝替他人说话的人，于是有了「代祷」之义。

intro.en: Intercede comes from Latin intercedere, to go between or to intervene, built from inter, between, and cedere, to go.
intro.cn: intercede 来自拉丁语 intercedere（走在中间、介入），由 inter（在……之间）加 cedere（走）构成。

items.en: Intercedere is formed from inter, between, and cedere, to go, with the image of stepping into the middle.
items.cn: intercedere 由 inter（在……之间）与 cedere（走）构成，画面是走进中间。

items.en: In Roman law the verb also means to interfere and to veto an act by intervening.
items.cn: 在罗马法中，这个动词还有「干预」之意，并因介入而否决某一行为。

items.en: The modern sense shades from mediation toward asking God for mercy, the root of the idea of intercession.
items.cn: 这一义项从「调解」进一步偏向请求上帝宽恕，成为「代祷」一词的根源。

items.en: Intercede enters English in the sixteenth century with the sense of pleading for another.
items.cn: intercede 于十六世纪进入英语，义为替他人求情。

items.en: Today the word covers polite appeals, quiet diplomacy, and church prayers for others.
items.cn: 如今该词涵盖客气的求情、低调的外交斡旋与教堂里的代祷。

note.en: Intercede is the between-going verb: close to intercession, intermediary, and to everyday words for pleading and mediation.
note.cn: intercede 是一个表示「走在中间」的动词，与 intercession、intermediary 同族，也和求情、调解类日常词相邻。

entries.definition: the act of pleading for someone else
entries.definitionCN: 替他人求情或斡旋的行为

entries.definition: a person who pleads for others
entries.definitionCN: 代他人求情或调解的人

entries.definition: to admit or yield
entries.definitionCN: 承认；让步（与 intercede 共享拉丁语词根 cedere）

entries.definition: to help two sides reach agreement
entries.definitionCN: 调解；居间调停（重在促成和解）

entries.definition: to ask for something in an urgent way
entries.definitionCN: 恳求；辩护（更直接地表达请求）

entries.definition: to settle a dispute as an independent judge
entries.definitionCN: 仲裁；公断（以裁判身份作出裁决）

entries.definition: to step into a situation to change its course
entries.definitionCN: 介入；干预（重在有行动介入，不一定求情）

normalIntro.en: Intercede is the verb of going between: inter plus cedere, to go, with a speaker standing for another person.
normalIntro.cn: intercede 表示「走进去」：inter 加 cedere（走），画面是一个说话人站在另一个人前面。

normal.en: Intercede takes two prepositions: intercede with the judge, intercede for the prisoner.
normal.cn: intercede 常配两个介词：向法官求情，为犯人求情。

normal.en: The noun intercession and the person intercessor shorten the same idea.
normal.cn: 名词 intercession 和人物名词 intercessor 都承载同一个意思。

normal.en: The root cedere, to go, also appears in concede and proceed.
normal.cn: 词根 cedere（走）也出现在 concede 与 proceed 中。

normal.en: Intercede in a dispute, but intercede for a person.
normal.cn: 在争端中用 in，为人求情用 for。

normal.en: Compare mediate: mediate works on both sides, intercede usually speaks for one.
normal.cn: 对比 mediate：mediate 兼顾双方，intercede 通常只替一方说话。

abstract.en: Picture a thin figure slipping between two shouting people and raising one hand.
abstract.cn: 想象一个瘦小的身影挤进两个吵架的人中间，举起一只手。

abstract.en: See a lawyer walking into a courtroom to ask the king for mercy on a stranger.
abstract.cn: 想象一位律师走进法庭，替一个陌生人向国王讨要宽恕。

abstract.en: Hear a soft voice praying for a sick friend in a quiet chapel.
abstract.cn: 想象安静的礼拜堂里，有一个轻柔的声音在为生病的朋友祈祷。

examples.en: The manager interceded for the young worker and saved his job.
examples.cn: 经理替那位年轻的工人说情，保住了他的工作。

examples.en: Several countries asked the mediator to intercede before talks collapsed.
examples.cn: 在谈判破裂之前，几个国家请求调解人出面斡旋。

examples.en: When tempers rose, an old friend interceded and calmed both sides.
examples.cn: 气氛紧张时，一位老朋友出面劝解，平息了双方。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因他死得」——因为「他死得」冤枉，有人站出来替他说情；这只是拆音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 inter（在……之间）+ cedere（走）→ intercedere（走在中间、介入）→ 英语 intercede，核心义「站到冲突双方之间出声」。

sensesIntro.en: Intercede starts from going between two people to speak for one of them, widens to mediating a whole dispute, and in religious use becomes pleading with God.
sensesIntro.cn: intercede 从「走到两人之间替一方说话」出发，扩展为调停整场争端，在宗教用法中又变成向上帝代求。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person stepping between two sides to speak for the weaker one.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人走到冲突双方之间，替较弱的一方说话。

branches.en: Speaking for one person is the basic sense.
branches.cn: 替一方说话是最基本的义项。

branches.en: Handling the whole quarrel is the diplomatic sense.
branches.cn: 处理整场争执是外交式斡旋的义项。

branches.en: Addressing God for others is the religious sense.
branches.cn: 向上帝替他人祈求是宗教义项。

branches.en: Both pleading and mediating share the image of standing in the middle.
branches.cn: 求情与调解共享「站在中间」的意象。

branches.en: Mediation and intercession both urge a third party to act more gently.
branches.cn: 调解与代祷都在劝说第三方更宽容地对待他人。

intro.en: Intercede is built from the Latin prefix inter- and the root -cede, to go, and English forms intercession, intercessor, and intercessory around it.
intro.cn: intercede 由拉丁语前缀 inter- 与词根 -cede（走）构成，英语围绕它构成 intercession、intercessor 与 intercessory。

latinIntro.en: Latin inter means between, cedere means to go, and intercedere means to go between or to intervene.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 inter 意为「在……之间」，cedere 意为「走」，intercedere 意为「走在中间、介入」。

items.example: The prefix inter- puts a person between two sides.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 inter- 把一个人放到双方之间。

items.example: The root -cede supplies the movement in intercede.
items.exampleCN: 词根 -cede 为 intercede 提供「走」的动作。

items.example: Intercedere is the direct source of the English verb.
items.exampleCN: intercedere 是英语该动词的直接来源。

items.meaningCN: 构成源自拉丁语的动词
items.example: The final -e carries the Latin verb into English.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -e 把拉丁语动词带入英语。

items.meaningCN: 行为或结果的名词后缀
items.example: The suffix -ion forms intercession.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ion 构成 intercession。

items.meaning: the act of pleading for another
items.example: Intercession names the act itself.
items.exampleCN: intercession 指说情这一行为。

items.example: The suffix -or forms intercessor.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -or 构成 intercessor。

items.meaning: a person who pleads for others
items.example: An intercessor speaks for someone else.
items.exampleCN: 调解人替别人说话。

items.example: The suffix -ory forms intercessory.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ory 构成 intercessory。

items.example: Intercessory prayer asks for others.
items.exampleCN: 代祷是为他人祈求。

definition_zh: 对讲系统；内部通话设备
definition_en: a small device or system that lets people speak to each other inside a building, a vehicle, or a group of offices
core_image: 门口墙上的小盒子一按，屋里就传出说话声
scene: 访客站在公寓门口，按下墙上的白色小盒子，问楼上的人能不能开门。A visitor stood at the apartment entrance and pressed the white intercom to ask the family upstairs to open the door.
sceneCN: 这里 intercom 是「对讲设备」（第 1 个义项：住宅或办公场所门口用于内部通话的装置）；句意：访客站在公寓门口，按下墙上的白色小盒子，问楼上的人能不能开门。

pos.zh: 对讲系统；内部通话设备
对讲机的（用于修饰具体部件）

derivatives.zh: 由 inter- 加 communication 构成，义为「相互通信」，intercom 即其缩合词
由 inter- 加 communicate 构成，义为「互相通信、彼此联系」
由 intercom 加 system 构成的复合词，义为「对讲系统」

senses.title: A door-entry talk box
senses.titleCN: 门口对讲机；门禁对讲器
senses.definition: the small device by an entrance that lets a visitor talk to someone inside before the door is opened
senses.definitionCN: 装在入口处的小装置，让访客在开门前与屋内的人通话
senses.example: She checked who rang before answering the intercom.
senses.exampleCN: 她先看清是谁按了铃，才回应对讲机。
senses.why: The word is short for intercommunication, so its first job is simply to carry a voice from one part of a building to another.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是 intercommunication 的缩略，所以它最初的作用就是把声音从楼的一处传到另一处。

senses.title: An internal office or factory link
senses.titleCN: 内部通话系统；办公对讲
senses.definition: a wired or wireless system that connects rooms, desks, or machines within one workplace
senses.definitionCN: 把一个工作场所里的房间、工位或机器连接起来的内部通话系统
senses.example: The supervisor called the loading bay on the intercom.
senses.exampleCN: 主管用对讲系统呼叫了装卸区。
senses.why: From one door the same wiring spreads through a whole building, so the word names any closed network for inside talk.
senses.whyCN: 从一扇门出发，同样的线路可以铺满整栋楼，所以这个词也可指任何封闭的内部通话网络。

senses.title: A one-way public announcement channel
senses.definition: a loudspeaker channel, as in a school, train, or aircraft, used to give short messages to many listeners at once
senses.definitionCN: 在学校、火车或飞机上用来同时向许多人播放简短通知的喇叭通道
senses.example: The conductor used the intercom to announce the next stop.
senses.exampleCN: 列车员通过对讲广播报出下一站。
senses.why: Once voices travel along fixed lines, the same channel is handy for broadcasting one message to everyone inside.
senses.whyCN: 既然声音沿着固定线路走，同一条通道自然也可以把同一条消息播给里面所有人。

intro.en: Intercom is a twentieth-century blend of inter- and communicating, built on the model of intercommunication.
intro.cn: intercom 是二十世纪由 inter- 与 communicating 缩合而成的词，仿照 intercommunication 的构词方式。

items.en: Inter, meaning between, plus communicare, to share, already carries the idea of sharing something with another.
items.cn: inter（在……之间）加 communicare（共同分享），已经包含「与他人分享」的意思。

items.en: Communicate keeps the sense of sharing, and combine, conjoin, and conflict later build on the same combine-and-shorten pattern.
items.cn: communicate 保留了「分享」之义，combine、conjoin、conflict 等词后来也采用同样的「合并缩短」模式。

items.en: The noun intercommunication in the sense of two-way telephone service appears by the late nineteenth century.
items.cn: 意思是「双向通话服务」的名词 intercommunication 在十九世纪后期已经出现。

items.en: Intercom is recorded in the early twentieth century as a commercial and military term, then as the household word for a door-entry phone.
items.cn: intercom 在二十世纪初作为商业和军事术语见于记录，后来成为门口对讲机的日常叫法。

items.en: Today intercom covers school announcements, train carriages, lift phones, and factory linkups.
items.cn: 如今 intercom 既指校园广播，也指列车车厢、电梯对讲和工厂内部联线。

note.en: Intercom is a shortened compound, so it sits beside intercommunication, telephone, and other words for shouting across a small space.
note.cn: intercom 是缩合复合词，它与 intercommunication、telephone 同族，也与其他小范围传话词相邻。

entries.definition: two-way communication, especially by telephone
entries.definitionCN: 双向通信，尤指电话通信

entries.definition: to share information
entries.definitionCN: 交流；传达（intercom 缩短自 communicating）

entries.definition: between continents
entries.definitionCN: 洲际的（同样以 inter- 开头，与内部通话无关）

entries.definition: a device for speaking to someone far away
entries.definitionCN: 电话（用于与远方的人通话）

entries.definition: the old British name for radio broadcasting
entries.definitionCN: 无线电；旧式英式广播（与 intercom 同为早期无线设备名词）

entries.definition: a set of speakers for addressing a crowd
entries.definitionCN: 扩音广播系统（面向人群播报）

normalIntro.en: Intercom is inter plus com, the sound of talking between the walls of one building.
normalIntro.cn: intercom 就是 inter 加 com，是同一栋建筑里墙与墙之间通话的声音。

normal.en: Com here is not comedy but communicate, cut down to keep the word short.
normal.cn: 这里的 com 并非「喜剧」，而是 communicate 的缩短形式。

normal.en: Say intercom system when you mean the whole wiring, and just intercom for the box by the door.
normal.cn: 指整套线路时说 intercom system，指门上那个盒子时只说 intercom。

normal.en: The prefix inter- marks talk that stays between two points, never going outside.
normal.cn: 前缀 inter- 表明这种通话只在两点之间进行，不对外。

normal.en: Over the intercom is the fixed phrase for an announcement from a speaker.
normal.cn: over the intercom 是表示「通过对讲广播」的固定说法。

normal.en: Compare telephone: a telephone talks to the world, an intercom talks within a building.
normal.cn: 对比 telephone：电话对世界说话，对讲机只在楼里说话。

abstract.en: Picture a finger pressing a metal button, and a tiny speaker answering back.
abstract.cn: 想象一根手指按下金属按钮，一个小喇叭立刻回话。

abstract.en: Imagine a thin wire running through the walls from the gate to the kitchen.
abstract.cn: 想象一根细线穿过墙壁，把大门口和厨房连在一起。

abstract.en: Hear a tinny voice announcing the next station on a moving train.
abstract.cn: 想象列车上一个金属质感的声音报出下一站。

examples.en: The receptionist used the intercom to tell me that my guest had arrived.
examples.cn: 接待员用对讲机告诉我客人已经到了。

examples.en: A tired voice answered through the intercom and told us to wait outside.
examples.cn: 对讲机里传来一个疲惫的声音，让我们在外面等着。

examples.en: The factory installed new intercoms so that the two workshops could talk.
examples.cn: 工厂安装了新的对讲设备，好让两个车间能互相通话。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「音特康」——屋外阿康按「音」，屋内传音，靠的就是这台对讲机；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: inter-（在……之间）+ communicating（通信）缩合 → intercommunication 的简称 → 英语 intercom，核心义「楼内、车内两点之间的传话」。

sensesIntro.en: Intercom begins as one door box for a visitor, then widens to a whole workplace network, and finally to a loudspeaker that announces to everyone at once.
sensesIntro.cn: intercom 从门口一个供访客通话的盒子出发，扩展为由工位和房间组成的整栋内部网络，最后又指面向所有人播报的广播对讲。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small box by the door that carries a voice inside.
core.cn: 核心意象：门口一个小盒子，把声音传进屋里。

branches.en: The door-entry device is the most common sense.
branches.cn: 门口对讲器是最常见的义项。

branches.en: A workplace network is the extended sense.
branches.cn: 工作场所的内部网络是扩展义项。

branches.en: Broadcasting to a crowd is the loudspeaker sense.
branches.cn: 向人群播报是喇叭式义项。

branches.en: A door box and an office network both carry talk inside one building.
branches.cn: 门禁对讲与办公网络都是在同一栋楼内传话。

branches.en: Both a factory link and a train announcement reach people who share one closed space.
branches.cn: 厂内联线与列车广播都把消息传给处在同一封闭空间里的人。

intro.en: Intercom is an English blend of the Latin prefix inter- and the verb stem communicate; its family includes intercommunication.
intro.cn: intercom 是英语中由拉丁语前缀 inter- 与动词词干 communicate 缩合而成的词，同族词有 intercommunication。

latinIntro.en: Latin inter means between, and communicare means to share, so the pair gives the sense of sharing a voice between two points.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 inter 意为「在……之间」，communicare 意为「共同分享」，两者合起来就是「在两点之间共享声音」。

items.example: The prefix inter- marks talk inside one building.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 inter- 标记「楼内」的通话。

items.example: Communicare gives English communicate.
items.exampleCN: communicare 演变为英语 communicate。

items.example: Communicate is the verb behind the short form.
items.exampleCN: communicate 是这个缩略词背后的动词。

items.example: Intercom shortens intercommunication.
items.exampleCN: intercom 是 intercommunication 的缩短形式。

items.example: The piece com- keeps the word short.
items.exampleCN: com- 这一部分让词形更短。

items.meaningCN: 做某事的物或人的后缀
items.example: The suffix -er forms communicator.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -er 构成 communicator。

items.example: Communication shares the root of intercom.
items.exampleCN: communication 与 intercom 同根。

items.meaningCN: 行为或状态的名词后缀
items.example: The suffix -tion forms communication.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -tion 构成 communication。

items.example: The suffix -ate forms communicate.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ate 构成 communicate。

definition_zh: 相互依存；相互依赖的
definition_en: depending on each other, so that each person or part needs the others to work or to live well
core_image: 两个人互相扶着走，谁松手谁都会摔倒
scene: 小岛上种菜的人需要渔夫的鱼，渔夫又需要他的菜，两边谁也离不开谁。On the small island the farmer needed the fisher for fish, and the fisher needed the farmer for vegetables, so the two were interdependent.
sceneCN: 这里 interdependent 是「相互依存的」（第 1 个义项：双方彼此需要、互为依靠）；句意：小岛上种菜的人需要渔夫的鱼，渔夫又需要他的菜，两边谁也离不开谁。

pos.zh: 相互依存的；相互依赖的

derivatives.zh: 由 interdependent 去尾加 -ce 构成，义为「相互依存、相互依赖」
由 depend 加后缀 -ency 构成，义为「依赖；从属」
由 depend 加 -able 构成，义为「可靠的、可信赖的」
由 interdependence 加 theory 构成的学术复合词，义为「互依理论」

senses.title: Mutually reliant people
senses.definition: describing people or groups that each need the other in order to live, work, or feel secure
senses.definitionCN: 形容人或群体彼此都需要对方，才能生活、工作或获得安全感
senses.example: The two villages grew interdependent, trading fish for grain.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个村庄逐渐相互依存，以鱼换粮。
senses.why: The prefix inter- means one another and pendere means to hang, so two things that hang from each other cannot stand alone.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 inter- 表示「彼此」，pendere 表示「悬挂」，两样东西互相悬挂，谁也不能单独立着。

senses.title: Linked parts of a system
senses.definition: describing parts of a system, such as machines, industries, or ecosystems, that only work properly when they work together
senses.definitionCN: 形容机器、产业、生态系统等系统的组成部分，只有协同运作才能正常发挥
senses.example: In a rainforest every plant and insect is interdependent with its neighbours.
senses.exampleCN: 在雨林里，每种植物和昆虫都与周围的伙伴相互依存。
senses.why: Once the image leaves people and enters a system, the hanging links become the connections that hold a whole machine together.
senses.whyCN: 当意象从人扩展到系统时，悬挂的连接就变成把整台机器撑起来的各种关联。

senses.title: Shared fates across nations
senses.definition: describing countries or economies whose actions affect one another, so that a problem in one quickly reaches the rest
senses.definitionCN: 形容国家或经济体彼此的行动互相影响，一个地方的问题很快波及其余
senses.example: Modern economies are deeply interdependent, so a crisis never stays in one country.
senses.exampleCN: 现代经济体彼此高度依赖，因此危机从不停留在一国之内。
senses.why: What is true of two neighbours becomes a picture of the world once trade and finance tie every nation to the next.
senses.whyCN: 当贸易和金融把每个国家连到下一个国家，两个邻居之间的道理就成了整个世界的写照。

intro.en: Interdependent joins the Latin prefix inter-, one another, to dependent, which rests on pendere, to hang.
intro.cn: interdependent 由拉丁语前缀 inter-（彼此）与 dependent 组合而成，dependent 源自 pendere（悬挂）。

items.en: Pendere means to hang or weigh, and its participle gives the image of something hanging from a support.
items.cn: pendere 意为「悬挂、称量」，其分词形式带来「从支撑处挂着」的意象。

items.en: Dependere means to hang down from something, and from this comes the idea of relying on another.
items.cn: dependere 意为「从某物上垂挂下来」，由此引申出「依靠他人」的含义。

items.en: Dependre carries the verb into French with the sense of depending on someone.
items.cn: dependre 把这一动词带入法语，表示依赖某人。

items.en: Dependent is well established, and interdependent appears as a coined compound of inter- plus dependent.
items.cn: dependent 已经稳固，interdependent 作为 inter- 加 dependent 的合成词出现。

items.en: The word spreads through biology and economics, describing species webs and global trade.
items.cn: 该词通过生物学和经济学传播开来，用来描述物种之网与全球贸易。

note.en: Interdependent is the two-way form of dependent: close to interdependence and dependence, and to words for connection and reliance.
note.cn: interdependent 是 dependent 的双向形式：与 interdependence、dependence 同族，也和表示联系与依靠的词相邻。

entries.definition: the state of needing each other
entries.definitionCN: 相互依存的状态

entries.definition: needing someone or something else
entries.definitionCN: 依赖的（单向依赖，与 interdependent 相对）

entries.definition: reliable, able to be trusted
entries.definitionCN: 可靠的（同根，但义为「值得依靠」）

entries.definition: coming between two stages
entries.definitionCN: 中间的（同以 inter- 开头，只是拼写相近，词义无关）

entries.definition: felt or done by two sides equally
entries.definitionCN: 相互的（强调对等，不强调离不开）

entries.definition: depending on someone or something
entries.definitionCN: 依赖的（多为单向）

entries.definition: linked or joined together
entries.definitionCN: 相互关联的（强调联系，不一定彼此依赖）

normalIntro.en: Interdependent is inter, one another, plus dependent, hanging from something, so both sides hang from each other.
normalIntro.cn: interdependent 就是 inter（彼此）加 dependent（悬挂在某物上），于是两边互相悬挂。

normal.en: Start from depend, which goes back to Latin pendere, to hang.
normal.cn: 从 depend 入手，它可追溯到拉丁语 pendere（悬挂）。

normal.en: Add the prefix inter- and one-way dependence becomes two-way.
normal.cn: 加上前缀 inter-，单向依赖就变成双向依赖。

normal.en: The noun is interdependence, with -ce instead of -t.
normal.cn: 名词形式是 interdependence，词尾是 -ce 而非 -t。

normal.en: Keep the word after a linking verb: the two are interdependent, not interdependent each other.
normal.cn: 这个词用作表语：the two are interdependent，不接 each other。

normal.en: Keep the -ent spelling apart from independent, which means free of others.
normal.cn: 注意 -ent 的拼写，别和 independent（不依赖他人）混淆。

abstract.en: Picture two climbers roped together on a steep slope.
abstract.cn: 想象两个登山者用绳子系在一起，站在陡坡上。

abstract.en: Think of gears in a clock: turn one and the rest must follow.
abstract.cn: 想象钟表里的齿轮：转动一个，其余的都随之而动。

abstract.en: See a bee on a flower, and the flower waiting for the bee.
abstract.cn: 想象蜜蜂停在花上，而花也在等着蜜蜂。

examples.en: In a healthy marriage the two partners are interdependent rather than competitive.
examples.cn: 在健康的婚姻里，伴侣双方相互依存，而不是彼此竞争。

examples.en: Modern supply chains are so interdependent that one closed port slows the whole world.
examples.cn: 现代供应链彼此高度依赖，一个港口关闭就会拖慢整个世界。

examples.en: The interdependence of these species has been studied for decades.
examples.cn: 这些物种之间的相互依存关系已被研究了几十年。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因特弟碰等特」——弟弟们「碰」在一起互相「等」着，谁也不能先走；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 inter（彼此）+ pendere（悬挂）→ dependere（从某物垂挂、依赖）→ depend / dependent → 加前缀 inter- 构成 interdependent，核心义「互相挂着，谁也不能单独站着」。

sensesIntro.en: Interdependent begins with people who need each other, moves to linked parts of a system, and finally to nations whose fortunes are tied together.
sensesIntro.cn: interdependent 先指彼此需要的人，再指系统中相互关联的部件，最后指命运相连的国家与经济体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two people propping each other up, and either one falling if the other lets go.
core.cn: 核心意象：两人互相扶着走，谁松手谁都会摔倒。

branches.en: People who need each other are the basic sense.
branches.cn: 彼此需要的人是基本义项。

branches.en: Parts of a working system form the mechanical sense.
branches.cn: 运作系统中的部件构成系统义项。

branches.en: Nations with linked fortunes form the global sense.
branches.cn: 命运相连的国家构成全球义项。

branches.en: Both a neighbour and a trading partner rely on the other to flourish.
branches.cn: 邻居与贸易伙伴都要靠对方才能兴旺。

branches.en: An ecosystem and a world economy both fail together when one part breaks.
branches.cn: 生态系统与世界经济都可能在某一部件出问题时一起失灵。

intro.en: Interdependent is the Latin prefix inter-, one another, plus the adverb dependens and its verb depend, so English also forms interdependence.
intro.cn: interdependent 是拉丁语前缀 inter-（彼此）与 depend 及其分词组合而成，英语另有名词 interdependence。

latinIntro.en: Latin inter means one another and pendere means to hang, so dependere means to hang from and hence to rely on something.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 inter 意为「彼此」，pendere 意为「悬挂」，dependere 意为「从某物垂下」，进而表示依靠。

items.example: The prefix inter- turns one-way reliance into two-way.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 inter- 把单向依赖变成双向依赖。

items.example: Pendere gives the picture of something hanging from a support.
items.exampleCN: pendere 带来「从支撑处悬挂」的画面。

items.meaning: to hang down from, to rely on
items.example: Dependere is the ancestor of depend.
items.exampleCN: dependere 是 depend 的祖先。

items.example: Depend is the base verb of the family.
items.exampleCN: depend 是这一词族的基词。

items.meaningCN: 形容词后缀，表示「处于……状态」
items.example: The suffix -ent forms dependent.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ent 构成 dependent。

items.example: Dependent is the adjective that inter- modifies.
items.exampleCN: dependent 是被 inter- 修饰的形容词。

items.meaningCN: 状态或性质的名词后缀
items.example: The suffix -ence forms interdependence.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ence 构成 interdependence。

items.meaning: the state of needing each other
items.example: Interdependence names the state, not the relation.
items.exampleCN: interdependence 指一种状态，而非一对关系。

items.example: Independent is the -ent word that is not formed with inter-.
items.exampleCN: independent 是不带 inter- 的 -ent 形容词。

items.example: The suffix -able forms dependable.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -able 构成 dependable。

latinEntries.meaning: to hang down from, to depend on

definition_zh: 星际的；星系间的
definition_en: existing or happening between galaxies, or relating to the space that separates them
core_image: 两团旋涡星云之间那条空荡荡的深黑长路
scene: 天文学家把望远镜对准两团星云之间的空域。The astronomers pointed the telescope at the intergalactic void between two galaxies.
sceneCN: 这里 intergalactic 是「星系间的」（第 1 个义项：星系与星系之间的空域；中文铺垫里转写为「星系间的空域」）；句意：天文学家把望远镜对准了两团星系之间那片星系际的虚空。

pos.zh: 星际的；星系间的

derivatives.zh: 银河的；星系的，由希腊语 galaxias 加词尾 -ic 构成
星系；银河，来自希腊语「乳白色的路」
星际的，指恒星之间，由 inter- 加 stellar 构成
行星际的，指行星之间，由 inter- 加 planet 加 -ary 构成

senses.title: Between galaxies
senses.definition: located in the space that lies between one galaxy and another
senses.definitionCN: 位于一个星系与另一个星系之间的空间中的
senses.example: The gas clouds drift through intergalactic space.
senses.exampleCN: 气体云在星系际空间中飘移。
senses.why: The prefix inter- means between, and galactic means of a galaxy, so the word names the void that stretches between island universes.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 inter- 表示「在……之间」，galactic 表示「星系的」，所以这个词指的是各座「宇宙岛」之间那片空旷区域。

senses.title: Of the cosmos beyond galaxies
senses.definition: relating to travel, communication, or events that cross from one galaxy to another
senses.definitionCN: 与跨越星系之间的旅行、通信或事件有关的
senses.example: Science fiction loves stories about intergalactic voyages.
senses.exampleCN: 科幻小说喜欢讲星际远航的故事。
senses.why: Once the word names the space between galaxies, it easily extends to anything that moves across it, such as ships or signals.
senses.whyCN: 既然这个词先指星系之间的空间，就很容易再指穿越这片空间的事物，例如飞船或信号。

senses.title: Enormous in scale
senses.definition: extremely large, wide, or exaggerated in extent
senses.definitionCN: 范围极大、极广阔或明显夸张的
senses.example: The meeting ran on for what felt like an intergalactic length of time.
senses.exampleCN: 那场会议拖得漫长得不像话。
senses.why: Because the distance between galaxies is the very image of vastness, the adjective lends itself to humorous exaggeration of everyday things.
senses.whyCN: 星系之间的距离本身就是「巨大」的最好形象，所以这个形容词常用于调侃日常事物的夸张程度。

intro.en: Intergalactic joins Latin inter, meaning between, to galactic, an English adjective built on the Greek name for a galaxy.
intro.cn: intergalactic 由拉丁语 inter（在……之间）与英语形容词 galactic 组合而成，后者源自希腊语的「银河」一词。

items.en: Galaxias means milky, from gala, milk, and names the Milky Way.
items.cn: galaxias 意为「乳白色的」，来自 gala（奶），用来指称银河。

items.en: Inter means between, and the Latin name of the Milky Way is via lactea.
items.cn: inter 意为「在……之间」，而银河的拉丁语名称是 via lactea。

items.en: Galaxie enters English through Old French for the Milky Way.
items.cn: galaxie 经古法语进入英语，指银河。

items.en: Galactic is formed as an adjective, and other galaxies are recognized.
items.cn: galactic 作为形容词形成，天文学界也确认了银河系以外的其他星系。

items.en: Inter- and galactic are combined for the space between galaxies.
items.cn: 人们把 inter- 与 galactic 组合起来，指星系之间的空间。

items.en: The word is used for astronomy and, loosely, for science fiction and exaggeration.
items.cn: 现代英语里它既用于天文学，也用于科幻和夸张表达。

note.en: Intergalactic sits in a family of inter- compounds and belongs to the vocabulary of space and scale.
note.cn: intergalactic 属于 inter- 构成的复合词家族，也属于空间与尺度这一词汇场。

entries.definition: relating to a galaxy
entries.definitionCN: 银河的；星系的，与本词共享 galactic 词根

entries.definition: a very large group of stars
entries.definitionCN: 星系；银河，是本词的词根名词

entries.definition: relating to stars
entries.definitionCN: 星球的；恒星的，与 galactic 词根不同，只是同属天文字汇场

entries.definition: between the stars
entries.definitionCN: 恒星之间的；星际的

entries.definition: between planets
entries.definitionCN: 行星之间的；行星际的

entries.definition: relating to the whole universe
entries.definitionCN: 宇宙的；广大无边的

normalIntro.en: Split the word into inter, between, and galactic, of a galaxy: the space that lies in between.
normalIntro.cn: 把词拆成 inter（在……之间）与 galactic（星系的），合起来就是夹在中间的星系间空间。

normal.en: Inter- appears in international and internet, both about things that reach across.
normal.cn: inter- 出现在 international 与 internet 里，都与「跨越」有关。

normal.en: Galactic comes from the same Greek source as galaxy.
normal.cn: galactic 与 galaxy 来自同一个希腊语来源。

normal.en: Intergalactic space is the room between the islands of stars.
normal.cn: intergalactic space 就是星岛之间的空当。

normal.en: Compare interstellar, between stars, and interplanetary, between planets.
normal.cn: 对比 interstellar（恒星之间）与 interplanetary（行星之间），尺度依次放大。

normal.en: In science fiction the word marks the largest possible journey.
normal.cn: 在科幻作品里，这个词标记着最大的旅程尺度。

abstract.en: Picture two whirlpools in a dark sea with a long empty channel between them.
abstract.cn: 想象黑暗海洋里的两个旋涡，中间躺着一条长长的空水道。

abstract.en: Imagine a signal crossing from one island of lights to another.
abstract.cn: 想象一束信号从一座灯光岛飞向另一座灯光岛。

abstract.en: Hear someone say the trip took an intergalactic amount of time.
abstract.cn: 听见有人调侃说这趟行程花了星际般漫长的时间。

examples.en: Astronomers study hot gas in intergalactic space.
examples.cn: 天文学家研究星系际空间中的高温气体。

examples.en: The film follows an intergalactic journey to a distant star system.
examples.cn: 这部影片讲述了一段前往遥远恒星系的星际旅程。

examples.en: Intergalactic dust can dim the light of very distant galaxies.
examples.cn: 星系际尘埃会削弱极遥远星系的光。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因特＋ galactic」——因特网把世界各地连起来，inter- 也是「在……之间」，两个星系的「之间」就是 intergalactic；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 inter（在……之间）＋ 希腊语 galaxias（乳白色的环，指银河）＋ 英语形容词词尾 -ic → galactic → intergalactic，核心义「横跨在两座星系之间的」。

sensesIntro.en: Intergalactic first names the space between galaxies, then what crosses it, and finally anything ridiculously vast.
sensesIntro.cn: intergalactic 先指星系之间的空间，再指穿越这片空间的事物，最后引申为任何大得离谱的规模。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a dark empty channel running between two glowing galaxies.
core.cn: 核心意象：两团发光星系之间的一条黑暗空道。

branches.en: The literal sense is the space separating galaxies.
branches.cn: 字面义就是分隔各个星系的空间。

branches.en: Travel and signals extend the space sense to the crossing.
branches.cn: 旅行与信号把空间义延伸到「穿越」这一动作。

branches.en: Vastness turns the astronomical scale into playful exaggeration.
branches.cn: 巨大的尺度让天文学的度量变成俏皮的夸张。

branches.en: A crossing needs the space it crosses.
branches.cn: 一次跨越离不开它所穿越的那片空间。

branches.en: The gap between galaxies is the very picture of the enormous.
branches.cn: 星系之间的间隙正是「巨大」最直观的画面。

intro.en: Intergalactic is a compound of the prefix inter-, the root galactic, and the suffix -ic, with related words across space and scale.
intro.cn: intergalactic 是由前缀 inter-、词根 galactic 与词尾 -ic 组成的复合词，与空间和尺度上的相关词构成词族。

latinIntro.en: The prefix inter is Latin for between, while galactic comes from Greek galaxias, the milky circle of the sky.
latinIntro.cn: 前缀 inter 是拉丁语「在……之间」，galactic 则来自希腊语 galaxias，即天上的乳白色环带。

items.example: The prefix inter- marks what lies between two things.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 inter- 标示两件事物之间的位置。

items.example: The root galact- gives the milky image of the sky.
items.exampleCN: 词根 galact- 带来天上的乳白意象。

items.example: The suffix -ic turns galactic into an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ic 使 galactic 成为形容词。

items.example: A galaxy is an island of stars.
items.exampleCN: galaxy 就是一座星岛。

items.example: Galactic describes the scale of one galaxy.
items.exampleCN: galactic 描述一个星系内部的尺度。

items.example: Intergalactic names the gap between galaxies.
items.exampleCN: intergalactic 指星系之间的空隙。

items.example: Interstellar steps the scale down to stars.
items.exampleCN: interstellar 把尺度缩小到恒星之间。

items.example: Interplanetary moves the frame closer still.
items.exampleCN: interplanetary 把范围再拉近一步。

items.example: The same inter- shows up in international.
items.exampleCN: 同一个 inter- 也出现在 international 中。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 银河，字面为奶白色的路

definition_zh: 幕间曲；插曲；间歇；短暂的插曲式事件
definition_en: a short period or piece that comes between two longer parts of an event or performance
core_image: 两幕戏之间，乐队在拉上幕布的空当里轻轻奏起一段小曲
scene: 第二幕开演前，乐队奏起一段轻柔的幕间曲。Before the second act began, the orchestra played a gentle interlude.
sceneCN: 这里 interlude 是「幕间曲」（第 1 个义项：两幕戏之间表演的短乐曲）；句意：第二幕开演前，乐队奏起了一段轻柔的幕间曲。

pos.zh: 幕间曲；插曲；间歇；短暂插曲式时期

derivatives.zh: 幕间的；插曲的，由 interlude 加 -ial 构成
在……之间，是 interlude 的前半部分
嬉戏的；顽皮的，与拉丁语 ludere（玩耍）同源
前奏；序曲，与 interlude 同含拉丁语 ludus 与 -ium 词尾

senses.title: A short piece between acts
senses.definition: a short piece of music or a short performance given between the parts of a play or concert
senses.definitionCN: 在一出戏或一场音乐会各段之间演奏的短曲或短表演
senses.example: The organist played a quiet interlude between the scenes.
senses.exampleCN: 管风琴师在几场戏之间弹了一支安静的间奏曲。
senses.why: The Latin inter means between and ludus means play, so the word was first a play or tune staged in the gap between acts.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 inter 意为「在……之间」，ludus 意为「游戏、戏剧」，所以这个词本指在两幕之间上演的一小段戏或曲子。

senses.title: A pause between periods
senses.definition: a short period of time that separates two longer periods of activity or events
senses.definitionCN: 把两段较长的活动或事件隔开的短暂时间
senses.example: A short interlude of calm followed the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 暴风雨之后出现了一段短暂的平静。
senses.why: From a break on the stage, the word moves to any break in time, marked off from what comes before and after.
senses.whyCN: 从舞台上的停顿，这个词推广到时间上的任何停顿，把前后两段区分开来。

senses.title: A separate episode inside a long one
senses.definition: a short, distinct event or experience that stands out in the middle of a longer situation
senses.definitionCN: 在一段较长的经历中间独立出来、格外醒目的一段小事件
senses.example: Their year abroad was a happy interlude in a hard working life.
senses.exampleCN: 他们出国那一年，是辛苦工作生涯里一段愉快的插曲。
senses.why: Anything that interrupts the main flow, like music filling a gap between acts, can be called an interlude.
senses.whyCN: 凡是打断主线的短暂存在，如同幕间填补空当的音乐，都可以叫插曲。

intro.en: Interlude comes from Latin inter, between, and ludus, play, through the medieval Latin form interludium, a little play performed between the parts of a larger show.
intro.cn: interlude 源自拉丁语 inter（在……之间）与 ludus（游戏、戏剧），经中世纪拉丁语 interludium 传入英语，本指在一台大戏各段之间上演的小戏。

items.en: Ludus means play or game, and inter means between.
items.cn: ludus 意为游戏、戏剧，inter 意为「在……之间」。

items.en: Interludium names a short play or tune inserted between parts.
items.cn: interludium 指插入几段之间的小戏或短曲。

items.en: Interlude first appears for a dramatic or musical performance between courses or scenes.
items.cn: 英语中最早用 interlude 指宴席各道菜之间或各场戏之间的表演。

items.en: Interludes are short comic plays staged at court and in schools.
items.cn: 这一时期宫廷与学校里上演的短小喜剧也叫 interlude。

items.en: The sense widens to any quiet period sandwiched between busier ones.
items.cn: 现代英语里词义扩展到夹在繁忙时段之间的任何安静时期。

note.en: Interlude shares its Latin play root with prelude and inter- compounds, and sits near interval and episode in meaning.
note.cn: interlude 与 prelude 及 inter- 类复合词共享拉丁语「戏」的词根，意思上靠近 interval 与 episode。

entries.definition: a short piece played before something larger
entries.definitionCN: 前奏；序曲，与 interlude 同含拉丁语 ludus，但前缀表示「在前」

entries.definition: a closing piece of music
entries.definitionCN: 尾曲；后奏，与 interlude 同源但表示「在后」

entries.definition: absurdly funny
entries.definitionCN: 荒唐可笑的，与 ludus 同源，这里只是拼写相近

entries.definition: a period between two events
entries.definitionCN: 间隔；幕间休息

entries.definition: one event in a series
entries.definitionCN: 一段插曲；一集

entries.definition: a short pause in work
entries.definitionCN: 短暂的休息

normalIntro.en: Read interlude as inter plus lude: a little play slipped into the space between two acts.
normalIntro.cn: 把 interlude 读成 inter 加 lude：一段小戏被塞进两幕之间的空当。

normal.en: Inter- means between, as in international and internet.
normal.cn: inter- 表示「在……之间」，如 international 与 internet。

normal.en: Prelude comes first, interlude sits in the middle, postlude comes last.
normal.cn: prelude 在最前，interlude 居中，postlude 在最后。

normal.en: Operas often use an interlude to cover a change of scenery.
normal.cn: 歌剧常用幕间曲来掩护换景。

normal.en: A peaceful interlude breaks up a busy day.
normal.cn: a peaceful interlude 就是打断忙碌一天的平静空档。

normal.en: In a life story, an interlude stands out between two chapters.
normal.cn: 在人生故事里，插曲是夹在两章之间格外醒目的那一段。

abstract.en: Watch the curtain fall, then hear soft strings fill the dark.
abstract.cn: 看幕布落下，再听轻柔的弦乐填满黑暗。

abstract.en: Picture a short calm lake between two rushing rivers.
abstract.cn: 想象两条急流之间夹着一片安静的小湖。

abstract.en: See one bright, separate bead threaded between long grey beads.
abstract.cn: 想象一串灰珠中间穿进了一颗亮珠子。

examples.en: The album includes several short instrumental interludes.
examples.cn: 这张专辑收录了几段简短的器乐间奏曲。

examples.en: Between the long meetings there was a pleasant interlude of coffee and talk.
examples.cn: 长长的会议之间，有一段喝咖啡聊天的愉快间歇。

examples.en: He described his time in the village as a peaceful interlude.
examples.cn: 他把自己在村里的那段日子形容为一段平静的插曲。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因特＋lude」——因特网让你在两端之间来回切换，inter 正是「在……之间」，两幕之间那点空当就是 interlude；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 inter（在……之间）＋ ludus（游戏、戏剧）→ 中世纪拉丁语 interludium（戏与戏之间的小戏）→ 古法语 entrelude → 英语 interlude，核心义「夹在两段之间的一小段」。

sensesIntro.en: Interlude starts as a little play or tune between acts, widens to a pause in time, and finally to any separate episode inside a longer one.
sensesIntro.cn: interlude 从两幕之间的小戏小曲出发，扩展为时间上的停顿，最后指较长经历中任何独立出来的一段。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: soft music filling the dark gap while stage hands change the scenery.
core.cn: 核心意象：幕布落下、场上换景时，乐队用轻音乐填满那段黑暗的空当。

branches.en: The stage sense keeps the original idea of art between acts.
branches.cn: 舞台义保留了「两幕之间的一小段艺术」这一本义。

branches.en: The gap itself becomes a stretch of quiet time.
branches.cn: 那道空当本身变成一段时间上的安静停顿。

branches.en: Anything filling such a gap can be called a short episode.
branches.cn: 凡填进这个空当的东西，都可以叫一段插曲。

branches.en: A tune between acts is also a pause between the acts.
branches.cn: 幕间的小曲同时也是两幕之间的停顿。

branches.en: A quiet episode is a pause in the middle of busy life.
branches.cn: 一段平静的小插曲就是忙碌生活中的一次停顿。

intro.en: Interlude is built from the prefix inter-, the root lude from Latin ludus, and forms a family with prelude, postlude, and collude.
intro.cn: interlude 由前缀 inter- 与来自拉丁语 ludus 的词根 lude 构成，与 prelude、postlude、collude 组成词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin inter means between, and ludus means play or game, giving the stage sense of a little play in a gap.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 inter 意为「在……之间」，ludus 意为游戏、戏剧，合起来就是空当里的一段小戏。

items.example: The prefix inter- places the word in a gap.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 inter- 把词义放到两段之间的空当里。

items.example: The root lud- brings the idea of play.
items.exampleCN: 词根 lud- 带来「戏」的概念。

items.example: An interlude fills the space between two parts.
items.exampleCN: interlude 填满两部分之间的空当。

items.example: A prelude comes before, not between.
items.exampleCN: prelude 在前，而不在中间。

items.example: A postlude closes the performance.
items.exampleCN: postlude 为演出收尾。

items.example: Collude also carries the play root.
items.exampleCN: collude 同样带着这个「戏」的词根。

items.example: Illusion comes from the same playing root.
items.exampleCN: illusion 来自同一个「戏耍」词根。

items.example: The suffix -ial forms interludial.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ial 构成 interludial。

items.example: Interludial describes an in-between moment.
items.exampleCN: interludial 描述中间过渡的时刻。

definition_zh: 中间人；调解人；中介机构；中间的
definition_en: a person or organization that carries messages or arranges deals between two sides that do not meet directly
core_image: 站在两人之间，双手分别把话递给左边和右边的人
scene: 两家公司谈不拢，只好请一位中间人来回传话。The two firms could not agree, so they hired an intermediary to carry messages.
sceneCN: 这里 intermediary 是「中间人」（第 1 个义项：在双方之间传话或撮合的个人）；句意：两家公司谈不拢，于是请了一位中间人来回传话。

pos.zh: 中间人；调解人；中介机构
中间的；媒介的

derivatives.zh: 中间的；中级的，是 intermediary 的形容形式
中介作用；居间调停，由 intermediary 加 -ation 构成
调解；居间传达，与 medium 同源
媒介；中间物，是拉丁语 medius（中间的）的名词形式

senses.title: A go-between person
senses.definition: a person who carries messages or passes information between two sides who do not deal with each other directly
senses.definitionCN: 在彼此不直接交涉的双方之间传递消息或信息的个人
senses.example: She spoke to the landlord through an intermediary.
senses.exampleCN: 她通过一位中间人和房东交涉。
senses.why: The Latin medius means middle, so an intermediary is the person who stands in the middle and hands things across.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 medius 意为「中间的」，所以中间人就是站在正中、把东西递过去的人。

senses.title: A mediator in disputes
senses.definition: a person or body that helps two sides in a disagreement reach a settlement
senses.definitionCN: 帮助争执双方达成和解的个人或机构
senses.example: The union accepted the government as an intermediary in the talks.
senses.exampleCN: 工会同意由政府在谈判中充当调解人。
senses.why: A go-between who carries messages can also smooth out conflict, so the word covers formal mediating too.
senses.whyCN: 来回传话的中间人也常被用来缓和冲突，因此这个词也涵盖正式的调解。

senses.title: A middle organization
senses.definition: an organization such as a bank or broker that stands between savers, buyers, or sellers and handles deals for them
senses.definitionCN: 如银行或经纪商这类居中于储户、买方或卖方之间并代为处理交易的机构
senses.example: Banks are financial intermediaries that take deposits and make loans.
senses.exampleCN: 银行是吸收存款、发放贷款的金融中介机构。
senses.why: The same middle position scales up from a single person to an institution standing between two groups.
senses.whyCN: 同样的「居中」位置可以从一个人扩展到一家机构，站在两群人之间。

senses.title: Serving as a middle step
senses.definition: acting as an in-between stage, medium, or link rather than a final destination
senses.definitionCN: 充当过渡阶段、媒介或连接环节，而非最终归宿的
senses.example: The committee plays an intermediary role between the public and the council.
senses.exampleCN: 该委员会在公众与市政会之间起中介作用。
senses.why: When the noun stands in the middle for people, the adjective extends that middle position to stages, roles, and processes.
senses.whyCN: 名词指替人站在中间的位置，形容词则把这种中间位置推广到阶段、角色和过程上。

intro.en: Intermediary comes from Latin inter, between, and medius, middle, through the Latin verb intermediare and its modern French and English forms.
intro.cn: intermediary 源自拉丁语 inter（在……之间）与 medius（中间的），经拉丁语动词 intermediare 及近代法语、英语形式发展而来。

items.en: Medius means middle, and inter means between.
items.cn: medius 意为中间的，inter 意为「在……之间」。

items.en: Intermediarius and intermediare describe what lies or acts in between.
items.cn: intermediarius 与 intermediare 描述处在中间或起中间作用的事物。

items.en: Intermediaire appears as a noun and adjective for the middle position.
items.cn: 法语 intermediaire 作为名词与形容词表示中间位置。

items.en: Intermediary is borrowed for a person who mediates between sides.
items.cn: 英语借入 intermediary，用于指在双方之间斡旋的人。

items.en: Intermediary is applied to middle stages in science and commerce.
items.cn: 此后 intermediary 也用于科学和商业中的中间阶段。

items.en: Modern English uses it widely for finance, diplomacy, and law.
items.cn: 现代英语在金融、外交与法律领域广泛使用该词。

note.en: Intermediary belongs to a family built on Latin medius and sits near words for people and things in the middle.
note.cn: intermediary 属于以拉丁语 medius 为根的词族，意思上靠近各类表示「居中」的人或物。

entries.definition: in the middle between two levels
entries.definitionCN: 中间的；中级的，是本词同根形容词

entries.definition: a way of communicating
entries.definitionCN: 媒介；传播手段，与 medius 同源

entries.definition: to help settle a dispute
entries.definitionCN: 调停；居间调解，与本词共享 medius 词根

entries.definition: a person who arranges deals for others
entries.definitionCN: 经纪人；掮客，代他人撮合交易的人

entries.definition: a person who helps two sides agree
entries.definitionCN: 调解人，帮助双方达成一致的人

entries.definition: someone who passes messages between sides
entries.definitionCN: 中间人；传话的人，较为口语

normalIntro.en: Intermediary is inter plus mediary, from Latin medius, middle: the one who stands in the middle.
normalIntro.cn: intermediary 是 inter 加 mediary，来自拉丁语 medius（中间的）：站在正中间的那个人。

normal.en: Inter- means between, as in international and intervene.
normal.cn: inter- 表示「在……之间」，如 international 与 intervene。

normal.en: The med- part links to medium and mediate, all about the middle.
normal.cn: med- 这一部分连着 medium 与 mediate，都与「中间」有关。

normal.en: A bank is a financial intermediary between savers and borrowers.
normal.cn: 银行就是储户与借款人之间的金融中介。

normal.en: To act as an intermediary is to stand in for others.
normal.cn: act as an intermediary 就是替别人站在中间。

normal.en: The plural is intermediaries, with y changing to ies.
normal.cn: 复数 intermediaries，词尾 y 变 ies。

abstract.en: Picture a referee standing at the centre line passing a ball both ways.
abstract.cn: 想象裁判站在中线，把球向两边递。

abstract.en: See two people shouting across a wall while a third runs messages through a door.
abstract.cn: 想象两人隔着墙喊话，第三个人从门缝里来回递话。

abstract.en: Imagine money walking from a saver to a bank and then to a buyer.
abstract.cn: 想象钱先从储户走到银行，再从银行走到买家。

examples.en: The country agreed to talk only through an intermediary.
examples.cn: 该国同意只通过中间人进行谈判。

examples.en: Insurance brokers act as intermediaries between clients and companies.
examples.cn: 保险经纪人充当客户与保险公司之间的中介。

examples.en: Digital platforms have become powerful intermediaries in the music industry.
examples.cn: 数字平台已成为音乐产业中实力强大的中介。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因特＋mediary」——因特网把双方连在一起，中间那段「medi」正是媒介（medium）的核心，夹在中间传话的人就是 intermediary；这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 inter（在……之间）＋ medius（中间的）→ 拉丁语 intermediarius（居间的）→ 法语 intermediaire → 英语 intermediary，核心义「夹在双方正中、两头传递」。

sensesIntro.en: Intermediary begins with a person who carries messages, extends to a formal mediator, widens to institutions that stand in the middle, and ends as an adjective for anything in between.
sensesIntro.cn: intermediary 先指替人传话的中间人，扩大为正式调解者，再扩展到居中的机构，最后作形容词指任何处于中间的事物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one figure standing exactly in the centre, handing a message left and right.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人正站在正中，把消息分别递给左边和右边。

branches.en: The basic sense is a person who stands between and carries messages.
branches.cn: 基本义是站在双方之间传递消息的人。

branches.en: Smoothing conflict is a specialized job of the go-between.
branches.cn: 缓和冲突是中间人专门化的一项工作。

branches.en: Whole institutions now occupy the same middle position.
branches.cn: 如今整个机构占据了同样的居中位置。

branches.en: The adjective turns the position into a role or a stage.
branches.cn: 形容词把这个位置变成一种角色或阶段。

branches.en: All three nouns share the same risk and trust of standing in the middle.
branches.cn: 三个名词义项都共享「居中」带来的信任与风险。

intro.en: Intermediary combines the prefix inter-, the root medi- from Latin medius, and the suffix -ary, joining a family of medium, mediate, and intermediate.
intro.cn: intermediary 由前缀 inter-、来自拉丁语 medius 的词根 medi- 与词尾 -ary 组成，与 medium、mediate、intermediate 同属一个词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin inter means between and medius means middle, so a word built on both names exactly what sits in the centre.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 inter 意为「在……之间」，medius 意为中间的，两者合成的词正指位于中心之物。

items.example: The prefix inter- puts the word between two sides.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 inter- 把词义放在两方之间。

items.example: The root medi- carries the idea of the middle.
items.exampleCN: 词根 medi- 带来「中间」的概念。

items.meaning: a person or thing connected with
items.meaningCN: 与……有关的人或物的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ary forms a noun from the stem.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ary 由词干构成名词。

items.example: A medium is the channel in the middle.
items.exampleCN: medium 就是夹在中间的渠道。

items.meaning: to settle a dispute between sides
items.example: To mediate is to stand between and help.
items.exampleCN: mediate 就是站在中间帮忙。

items.meaning: in the middle of a scale
items.example: An intermediate level is midway between two others.
items.exampleCN: intermediate 水平介于另外两级之间。

items.meaning: the work of a middle party
items.example: Intermediation names the act of standing between.
items.exampleCN: intermediation 指居间中介的行为。

items.example: Median also keeps the middle image.
items.exampleCN: median 也保留着「中」的意象。

items.example: The rare adjective sense means indirect.
items.exampleCN: 较少见的形容词义表示间接的。

definition_zh: 混合；混淆；掺和；交错；杂处
definition_en: to mix things together so that their separate parts become combined
core_image: 两股不同颜色的沙，被一把铲子搅成一片
scene: 画家把两种颜料倒在调色板上，用画笔来回搅动，直到分不清界限。The painter intermixed the two colours on the palette until no edge remained.
sceneCN: 这里 intermix 是「混合、掺和」（第 1 个义项：把不同的东西搅在一起）；句意：画家在调色板上把两种颜料混到一起，直到看不出分界。

pos.zh: 使混合；使掺和；使混淆
混合；混杂；交错

derivatives.zh: inter-（在……之间）+ mingle（混）构成，义为「交错、混杂」，比 intermix 更强调彼此来往交织
intermix 加名词后缀 -ture 构成，义为「混合物；混杂状态」
intermix 加 -able 构成，义为「可混合的、能掺在一起的」

senses.title: To mix things together
senses.definition: to combine different things so that their parts are blended
senses.definitionCN: 把不同的东西合到一起，使各自的成分彼此融合
senses.example: The gardener intermixed sand with the soil to lighten it.
senses.exampleCN: 园丁把沙子掺进土里，让土变松。
senses.why: Inter- means between, and mix means to blend, so the word names blending things across their boundary.
senses.whyCN: inter- 表示「在……之间」，mix 表示搅混，所以这个词指把两边的成分搅到一起。

senses.title: To be mixed together naturally
senses.definition: to exist together in a mixed way, without keeping clear groups apart
senses.definitionCN: 不加区分地混在一起存在，不把不同的群分开
senses.example: The two communities intermix freely at the weekly market.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个群体在每周的集市上自由混杂来往。
senses.why: Because object and place both take the word, the mixing sense extends to people meeting and mingling.
senses.whyCN: 这个词既能带宾语也能自己出现，所以「混合」的意思自然延伸到人彼此来往、混在一起。

senses.title: To mix one thing into another
senses.definition: to add one kind of thing among another kind
senses.definitionCN: 把一类东西加进另一类东西之中
senses.example: She intermixed a few notes of humour with the serious report.
senses.exampleCN: 她在严肃的报告里夹杂了几处幽默。
senses.why: The between sense allows one thing to sit inside another, so intermix can mean adding something in.
senses.whyCN: 「在……之间」的含义允许一样东西嵌在另一样东西里，于是它也能表示往里面掺入。

senses.title: To confuse two things
senses.definition: to treat two separate things as if they were one
senses.definitionCN: 把两件本来分开的事情当成同一件
senses.example: Critics often intermix the two styles, though they are quite different.
senses.exampleCN: 评论家常把这两种风格混为一谈，其实它们差别很大。
senses.why: When things are blended until their borders vanish, the mind can no longer tell them apart; that is confusion.
senses.whyCN: 东西混到边界消失时，头脑就分不出彼此，这便是「混淆」。

senses.title: Interleaved or interspersed
senses.definition: arranged in a pattern where two kinds of things alternate rather than fully blend
senses.definitionCN: 两种东西按一定规律交替出现，而不是完全融成一体
senses.example: Bright and dark stones are intermixed along the path.
senses.exampleCN: 小路上亮石与暗石交错铺成。
senses.why: Even when parts do not dissolve, the between sense describes things set one among another in turn.
senses.whyCN: 即使成分并未真正融合，「在……之间」也能描述两种东西轮流穿插。

intro.en: Intermix joins the Latin prefix inter-, meaning between, to the verb mix, so it names mixing that happens between two or more things.
intro.cn: intermix 由拉丁语前缀 inter-（在……之间）加上动词 mix（混合）构成，指发生在两样或更多东西「之间」的混合。

items.en: Inter means between or among.
items.cn: inter 意为「在……之间」或在……之中。

items.en: Miscere means to mix; its noun mixtura names a mixed blend.
items.cn: miscere 意为混合，其名词 mixtura 指混合物。

items.en: Both elements reach English by way of French forms of inter and mesler.
items.cn: 两个成分都经由法语中的 inter 与 mesler 形式进入英语。

items.en: Mix is attested as a verb, and the prefix inter- is freely combined.
items.cn: mix 已作为动词见于中古英语，前缀 inter- 可自由组合。

items.en: Intermix is recorded from the sixteenth century, together with the noun intermixture.
items.cn: intermix 一般认为见于十六世纪，同时期还有名词 intermixture。

note.en: Intermix belongs to the inter- family of between words and sits close to everyday mix, blend and mingle.
note.cn: intermix 属于以 inter- 表示「之间」的词族，与日常的 mix、blend、mingle 相邻。

entries.definition: to mix together, especially in a way that invites mutual contact
entries.definitionCN: 交错；混杂（尤指彼此来往）

entries.definition: a mixture, or the state of being mixed
entries.definitionCN: 混合物；混杂状态

entries.definition: able to be mixed together
entries.definitionCN: 可混合的

entries.definition: to combine two or more things
entries.definitionCN: 混合；搅拌（最普通的说法）

entries.definition: to combine so smoothly that the parts cannot be separated
entries.definitionCN: （平稳地）混合；融合

entries.definition: to mix with other people or things, often in small amounts
entries.definitionCN: （少量）混杂；交往

normalIntro.en: Inter- gives the idea of between, so an intermix is a mix that happens between things that were kept apart.
normalIntro.cn: inter- 带来「之间」的画面，所以 intermix 就是原本分开的东西之间发生的混合。

normal.en: Inter- plus mix: things are mixed between each other.
normal.cn: inter- 加 mix：东西在彼此之间混了开来。

normal.en: Use intermix with: sand intermixed with soil.
normal.cn: 记住搭配 intermix with：沙子与土混在一起。

normal.en: The noun intermixture keeps the same idea of a blended thing.
normal.cn: 名词 intermixture 保留了「混成物」这一层意思。

normal.en: Compare mix, which is the everyday word; intermix often suggests two distinct parts coming together.
normal.cn: 对比 mix：mix 最日常，intermix 更强调两种原本分明的东西合到一起。

normal.en: Intermingle is the sibling verb for a looser, more personal mingling.
normal.cn: intermingle 是它的近义词，表示更松散、更带人情的交错。

abstract.en: Picture two streams of paint slowly curling into one swirl.
abstract.cn: 想象两道颜料缓缓卷进同一个涡流。

abstract.en: Imagine neighbours of two towns sharing one long table.
abstract.cn: 想象两个镇的邻居围坐在同一张长桌旁。

abstract.en: Think of a letter with a few jokes tucked between its serious lines.
abstract.cn: 想象一封信里在严肃的字句之间夹着几处玩笑。

examples.en: Farmers intermix several kinds of seed before planting.
examples.cn: 农民在播种前把几种种子掺在一起。

examples.en: In the old town, voices of many languages intermix.
examples.cn: 在古城里，多种语言的声音交织在一起。

examples.en: The report intermixes clear facts with open questions.
examples.cn: 这份报告把清楚的事实和悬而未决的问题夹杂在一起。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因特密克斯」——开头 inter 是「之间」，后半 mix 是「混合」，中间还带着「密切」的密；谐音里两层意思叠在一起，但这只是拆分联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 inter（在……之间）+ miscere（混合，经法语进入英语）→ 英语 mix → intermix，核心义「在两者之间把东西混到一起」。

sensesIntro.en: Intermix moves from physical blending, to people mixing freely, to adding one thing among another, to confusing two things, and finally to parts set in alternating order.
sensesIntro.cn: intermix 从实体上的掺和，扩展到人群自由混处、往里面掺入、把两件事混淆，最后还指两种成分交错排列。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two colours of sand turned into one patch.
core.cn: 核心意象：两色沙子被铲成一片分不清的沙。

branches.en: Blending two kinds into one body is the basic sense.
branches.cn: 把两种东西合成一体是最基本的义项。

branches.en: Free mixing grows into a shared-space sense about people.
branches.cn: 自由混合延伸出关于人群混处的共享空间义项。

branches.en: Adding one thing among another is the tuck-in sense.
branches.cn: 把一样东西掺进另一样是「掺入」义项。

branches.en: When borders vanish the mind confuses things, or sees them alternating.
branches.cn: 边界消失时，头脑会混淆两者，或只看到它们交错出现。

branches.en: Both mixing a batch and adding a little are ways parts meet between boundaries.
branches.cn: 整批混合与少量掺入都是成分在边界之间相遇的方式。

intro.en: Intermix is built from the prefix inter-, the verb mix, and the endings -ture and -able seen in its family.
intro.cn: intermix 由前缀 inter-、动词 mix，以及词族里出现的 -ture、-able 等词尾构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin inter means between, and miscere means to mix; the noun mixtura means a mixture.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 inter 意为在……之间，miscere 意为混合，名词 mixtura 意为混合物。

items.example: The prefix inter- tells you the mixing happens between things.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 inter- 告诉你混合发生在东西之间。

items.example: Latin miscere is the true source of the English verb to mix.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语 miscere 是英语动词 mix 的真正来源。

items.example: Mix is the everyday verb for blending several things.
items.exampleCN: mix 是表示混合的日常动词。

items.example: Mixtura gives the noun sense of a blended thing.
items.exampleCN: mixtura 提供「混成物」的名词含义。

items.meaning: result or state of an action
items.meaningCN: 表示行为结果或状态的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ture forms intermixture.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ture 构成 intermixture。

items.example: Intermixture names the result of mixing.
items.exampleCN: intermixture 指混合的结果。

items.example: The suffix -able forms intermixable.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -able 构成 intermixable。

items.example: Joining inter- and mix gives the word itself.
items.exampleCN: 把 inter- 和 mix 拼起来就是这个词本身。

items.example: Intermingle is the sibling verb of intermix.
items.exampleCN: intermingle 是 intermix 的同族动词。

items.example: Mingle is the base of intermingle.
items.exampleCN: mingle 是 intermingle 的词基。

definition_zh: 实习生；住院实习医师；拘留；软禁；作为实习生工作
definition_en: a student or trainee who works for experience, or to keep someone in a place and stop them leaving
core_image: 刚走出教室的年轻人，把工牌挂上胸前，跟在师傅身后
scene: 医学系的学生在医院里跟着主治医生查房，一边记录一边学习，期待毕业后留下。The medical student works as an intern in the hospital to learn from senior doctors.
sceneCN: 这里 intern 是「实习生」（第 1 个义项：为获得经验而在工作机构里跟班学习的人）；句意：这名医学生在医院当实习生，向资深医生学习。

pos.zh: 实习生；住院实习医师；被拘留者
拘留；软禁；（尤指在医院）当实习生

collocations.zh: 当实习生；以实习生身份工作

derivatives.zh: intern 加名词后缀 -ship 构成，义为「实习期；实习职位」
intern 加表示被动词后缀 -ee 构成，义为「被拘留者；被拘禁者」
intern 的动名词形式，义为「实习；被拘禁」，指持续进行的状态
取自 internus（内部）加 -ist（……的人），义为「内科医师」，专治内科疾病，不是实习生

senses.title: A trainee learning on the job
senses.definition: a student or recent graduate who works in an organisation for a fixed period to gain experience
senses.definitionCN: 学生或刚毕业的人在一家机构里工作一段时间以获得经验
senses.example: She joined the newspaper as a summer intern.
senses.exampleCN: 她以暑期实习生的身份加入这家报社。
senses.why: The basic sense is a person kept inside an institution for a time, so a learner placed inside an office fits the same picture.
senses.whyCN: 基本含义是「被留在某个机构里一段时间的人」，被安排进办公室学习的人正好符合同一个画面。

senses.title: A junior doctor in training
senses.definition: a recent medical graduate who is being trained in a hospital
senses.definitionCN: 刚从医学院毕业、在医院接受培训的初级医生
senses.example: The intern took the patient medical notes at midnight.
senses.exampleCN: 那位实习医生半夜记录了这个病人的病情。
senses.why: Hospitals were the first place where a temporary inside learner was given a formal title, so medicine keeps the oldest use.
senses.whyCN: 医院是最早把「暂留内部的学徒」正式命名的地方，所以医学保留了最古老的用法。

senses.title: To confine a person
senses.definition: to keep a person in a place, such as a camp or prison, and prevent them from leaving
senses.definitionCN: 把人关在营地或监狱之类的场所，不让他们离开
senses.example: During the war, the authorities interned thousands of civilians.
senses.exampleCN: 战争期间，当局拘留了数千名平民。
senses.why: The verb sense comes from the Latin idea of placing someone inside a boundary; being interned means being held within it.
senses.whyCN: 动词义来自拉丁语「把人放进某个范围里」的意思，被拘禁就是被留在范围之内。

senses.title: To work as a trainee
senses.definition: to work for a company or hospital for a period to learn the job
senses.definitionCN: 在公司或医院工作一段时间来学习这份工作
senses.example: He is interning at a law firm before he finishes his studies.
senses.exampleCN: 他在读完学位前在一家律师事务所实习。
senses.why: From the noun for the person, English made a verb meaning to do that work, so the trainee role became an action.
senses.whyCN: 英语由指人的名词派生出动词，表示做那份实习工作，于是「实习生身份」变成了动作。

senses.title: Detention as a measured punishment or restriction
senses.definition: the state of being confined for political or military reasons without a full trial
senses.definitionCN: 因政治或军事原因被限制自由、不经完整审判的关押状态
senses.example: The writer spent years under internment before friends spoke out.
senses.exampleCN: 这位作家在被拘禁多年之后，朋友们才公开为他发声。
senses.why: The confinement sense can be used for groups held for political reasons, which gives the word its charged modern tone.
senses.whyCN: 「限制在范围内」的意思可用于因政治原因被关押的群体，这给了它今天带有争议的语气。

intro.en: Intern comes from Latin internus, meaning inward or inside, which English first used for someone dwelling inside a school or hospital.
intro.cn: intern 来自拉丁语 internus（内部的、向内的），英语最初用它指住在学校或医院里的人。

items.en: Internus means inward, and the prefix inter marks what lies within.
items.cn: internus 意为向内的，前缀 inter 标示位于内部的东西。

items.en: French interne names a pupil who lives inside a boarding school.
items.cn: 法语 interne 指住在寄宿学校里的学生。

items.en: English uses intern for a resident pupil or student.
items.cn: 英语用 intern 指寄宿在学舍里的学生。

items.en: Medicine adopts intern for a resident house doctor in training.
items.cn: 医学界以 intern 指在医院住宿培训的住院医。

items.en: The verb sense of confining a person develops, and intern spreads to office trainees.
items.cn: 「关押某人」的动词义发展出来，intern 也扩展到办公室实习生。

note.en: Intern looks like internal and international, yet its core is simply inside, and it stands near trainee, apprentice and detain.
note.cn: intern 外形近似 internal 与 international，核心其实只是「在内部」，并与 trainee、apprentice、detain 相邻。

entries.definition: a period of trainee work inside an organisation
entries.definitionCN: 实习期；实习职位

entries.definition: happening or existing inside
entries.definitionCN: 内部的（由同一拉丁词根构成）

entries.definition: a person held as a prisoner by order
entries.definitionCN: 被拘留者；被拘禁者

entries.definition: a person being trained for a job
entries.definitionCN: 受训者；实习生（泛指）

entries.definition: a young worker learning a craft from a master
entries.definitionCN: 学徒（传统手艺）

entries.definition: to keep someone in official custody
entries.definitionCN: 扣留；拘留

normalIntro.en: Intern sits on the inside: Latin internus means inside, so an intern is a person kept inside a place to learn or held inside it by force.
normalIntro.cn: intern 的关键是「内部」：拉丁语 internus 意为内部的，所以 intern 指被留在机构里学习的人，或被强制留在里面的人。

normal.en: Inter- gives inside, so think of someone placed inside a school, hospital or camp.
normal.cn: inter- 带来「内部」之意：某人被安置在学校、医院或营地里面。

normal.en: Work as an intern is the most common modern pattern.
normal.cn: work as an intern 是现代最常见的搭配。

normal.en: The suffix -ship forms internship, the period of that work.
normal.cn: 后缀 -ship 构成 internship，指这段实习期。

normal.en: Compare trainee, which covers any trainee; intern is tied to a fixed placement inside an organisation.
normal.cn: 对比 trainee：trainee 泛指受训者，intern 专指在机构内部的一段固定实习。

normal.en: The verb sense to intern traps a person inside a boundary, while the noun keeps the learning side.
normal.cn: 动词义的 intern 是把人困在边界之内，名词义保留学习的一面。

abstract.en: Picture a new graduate pushing through the office door with a badge.
abstract.cn: 想象新毕业生戴着工牌推开办公室的门。

abstract.en: Picture a white coat passing along a hospital corridor at midnight.
abstract.cn: 想象深夜的医院走廊里走过一件白大褂。

abstract.en: Picture a fence line drawn around a group of people who cannot step out.
abstract.cn: 想象一道围栏圈住一群人，他们走不出去。

examples.en: Each intern is paired with a senior researcher.
examples.cn: 每位实习生都配一位资深研究员。

examples.en: The intern asked her mentor how to read the scan.
examples.cn: 这位实习医生请教导师如何看片子。

examples.en: Many villages were interned during that harsh winter.
examples.cn: 在那个严酷的冬天，许多村庄被整体拘禁。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因特恩」——因（因为）特（特别）恩（愿意留在里面）而留下的人；听起来像被留在机构内部的人，但这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 in（在内）+ inter（在……之间）→ internus（内部的）→ 法语 interne（寄宿学生）→ 英语 intern，核心义「被放在内部的人」。

sensesIntro.en: Intern begins with a resident trainee, narrows into the hospital doctor, widens into a temporary learner in any office, and then turns into the verbs of confining or acting as a trainee.
sensesIntro.cn: intern 从寄宿的学徒开始，缩窄到医院里的实习医生，再扩展到任何行业里的临时学习者，最后分出动词义：关押他人或自己去做实习生。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a badge on a chest and a name inside a closed door.
core.cn: 核心意象：胸前的工牌，以及关起的门里一个名字。

branches.en: A temporary learner inside an organisation is the working sense.
branches.cn: 机构里的临时学习者是最常用的义项。

branches.en: The hospital keeps the oldest formal sense.
branches.cn: 医院场景保留了最古老的正式义项。

branches.en: Being held inside a boundary grows into confinement.
branches.cn: 被留在边界之内延伸出「拘禁」与「软禁」。

branches.en: The noun for the person turns into a verb for the work.
branches.cn: 指人的名词转成了表示这份工作的动词。

branches.en: A trainee who interned is both a role and an action.
branches.cn: 实习的实习生既是角色也是动作。

intro.en: Intern is built on the Latin inside word internus, with -ship and -ee forming its common family.
intro.cn: intern 建立在拉丁语表示「内部」的 internus 之上，并以后缀 -ship、-ee 构成常用词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin internus means inward, from in and inter; it gives English internal, intern and international.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 internus 意为向内的，来自 in 与 inter，它给英语带来 internal、intern、international。

items.example: The prefix in- marks what is inside.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 in- 标示内部。

items.example: The prefix inter- shapes the Latin stem.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 inter- 塑造了这个拉丁语词干。

items.example: Internus is the direct source of the inside picture.
items.exampleCN: internus 是「内部」画面的直接来源。

items.example: The French noun brings the resident learner sense.
items.exampleCN: 法语名词带来「寄宿学习者」的含义。

items.example: Internship wraps the role in a period.
items.exampleCN: internship 把角色包进一段时间里。

items.meaningCN: 表示身份或时段的词尾
items.example: The suffix -ship forms internship.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ship 构成 internship。

items.example: The suffix -ee forms internee.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ee 构成 internee。

items.example: Internee means someone who is confined.
items.exampleCN: internee 指被关押的人。

items.example: Internal keeps the inside picture for things.
items.exampleCN: internal 把「内部」画面用在事物上。

items.example: Internist is a doctor, not a trainee.
items.exampleCN: internist 是医生，不是实习生。
